extra.message: Arbitrary code execution via eval() on user-controlled expression — Attacker can achieve arbitrary Python code execution on the server, leading to full system compromise, data exfiltration, or lateral movement. [verified: User-controlled GET parameter `expr` is passed directly to Python's eval(); restricted __builtins__ does not prevent escape via attribute access on provided locals (e.g., ().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()).]

Path traversal — user-controlled filename enables arbitrary file write — Attacker can write arbitrary content to any location on the filesystem reachable by the Django process, enabling code execution (overwriting Python files), configuration tampering, or denial of service. [verified: User-controlled GET parameter `name` is used directly in Path construction with write_bytes(), and parent directories are auto-created, allowing arbitrary file writes anywhere the Django process can reach.]

Server-side template injection via Jinja2 Template from user input — Attacker can execute arbitrary Python code on the server through Jinja2 template expressions, leading to full system compromise, data exfiltration, or remote code execution. [verified: User-controlled GET parameter `fragment` is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered, enabling arbitrary Python code execution through Jinja2 expression capabilities.]

CORS misconfiguration — reflected origin with credentials — Cross-origin requests from any malicious site can read sensitive JSON responses with the victim's credentials, enabling data theft via CSRF-style attacks. [verified: Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflects the request Origin header verbatim while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to true, allowing any malicious origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests.]

NoSQL injection via unsanitized JSON body as MongoDB query — Attacker can bypass query logic, extract arbitrary records, or potentially achieve code execution via `$where` JavaScript evaluation in MongoDB. [verified: User-supplied JSON body is used as a raw MongoDB query filter via find_one() without sanitization, enabling NoSQL operators like $where or $regex to bypass intended query logic.]

Hardcoded default Django SECRET_KEY — Complete compromise of session integrity, CSRF protection bypass, password reset token forgery, and ability to craft arbitrary signed cookies/tokens granting unauthorized access to any user account. [verified: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded string 'django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-in-production' when the env var is absent; no .env file, deployment config, or README instruction ensures it is overridden, so the default known-insecure key secures all session/CSRF/password-reset signing.]

Hardcoded Default Django SECRET_KEY — An attacker who discovers the default key can forge session cookies to impersonate any user, bypass CSRF protection, and decrypt signed data. [verified: SECRET_KEY falls back to 'django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-in-production' when SECRET_KEY env var is absent; no .env file or deployment configuration exists to override it, so the publicly known default key can forge all Django-signed data.]

Unrestricted file upload enabling stored XSS via media file serving — Attacker uploads a crafted HTML or SVG file with embedded JavaScript via the document upload form. Because DEBUG mode serves media/ directly, visiting the uploaded file's URL executes the script in the victim's browser in the application origin, enabling session hijacking, CSRF token theft, and arbitrary actions impersonating the victim (including staff users with elevated privileges). [verified: DocumentForm (forms.py:186) has zero file validation — no FileExtensionValidator, no clean_file, no content-type check; document_upload view (views.py:634) saves the raw file via form.save(); DEBUG=True is the default (settings.py:15), causing static() to serve MEDIA_ROOT at /media/ (urls.py:11-12) with native Content-Type, so an authenticated attacker's uploaded HTML/SVG executes script in the ap]

Missing rate limiting on login endpoint enabling brute-force — Attacker can perform unlimited password guessing attacks against any user account, potentially compromising credentials through dictionary or brute-force attacks. [verified: user_login has no rate-limiting decorator, middleware, lockout, or CAPTCHA; no django-ratelimit/axes/defender is installed, leaving the publicly reachable /login/ endpoint vulnerable to unlimited brute-force.]

IDOR — clinician can create prescriptions for unassigned patients — A clinician can prescribe medications for patients they are not authorized to treat, violating clinical scope boundaries and enabling unauthorized medical actions. [verified: PrescriptionForm patient queryset is all patients; prescription_create auto-sets provider but never validates the submitted patient against the clinician's assigned_patients, bypassing the _patient_or_403 guard used elsewhere.]

IDOR — clinicians can list all patients' PII beyond assigned scope — A clinician can view personal identifiable information (names, emails, insurance numbers) of all patients in the system, not just those assigned to them, violating horizontal access control and HIPAA data minimization principles. [verified: patient_list gates on is_staff_role (includes clinicians) but returns all PatientProfile rows with PII and no assigned_patients filter, unlike patient_detail which correctly calls _patient_or_403 to enforce clinician scope.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped GET parameter in ops HTML response — Attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript into the browser of anyone viewing the response, enabling session theft, credential phishing, or DOM manipulation. [verified: User-controlled GET parameter `copyline` is concatenated into HTML response without escaping; the _wrk_gate token check restricts who can reach the endpoint but does not neutralize the XSS sink.]

Open redirect via user-controlled redirect target — Phishing attacks — attacker crafts a URL that redirects victims to a malicious site while appearing to originate from the trusted clinic domain. [verified: User-controlled `lane` parameter is passed directly to Django's redirect() without any URL validation, enabling phishing via arbitrary external URLs.]

Sensitive data exposure — Authorization header written to logs — Bearer tokens and other Authorization header values are persisted in log files, accessible to anyone with log access, enabling credential theft and lateral movement. [verified: The raw Authorization header is logged via logger.warning to persistent file logs (settings.py configures RotatingFileHandler), exposing bearer tokens to anyone with log access.]

Ops endpoint patient_identity_ping_345 missing internal token gate check — Unauthenticated attackers can access an internal operational endpoint meant to be gated by INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN, enabling API reconnaissance and probing of internal endpoint behavior without any credential validation. [verified: patient_identity_ping_345 is the ONLY ops endpoint that does NOT call _wrk_gate(request); it is reachable without any x-internal-token check, exposing an internal operational endpoint to unauthenticated access.]

DEBUG mode enabled by default exposing sensitive information — Verbose error pages leak stack traces, environment variables, database credentials, SECRET_KEY, and server paths. Media files are served directly in DEBUG mode, potentially bypassing document access controls and exposing patient-uploaded clinical documents. [verified: DEBUG defaults to True with no .env override; verbose error pages would leak stack traces, local variables, SECRET_KEY, and DB credentials, and urls.py line 14 conditionally serves media files directly via static() bypassing document access controls.]

DEBUG mode enabled by default exposing verbose error pages — Sensitive configuration details, file paths, source code fragments, and database structure are exposed to unauthenticated users via error pages. [verified: DEBUG defaults to True at line 15 with no .env override; Django displays full stack traces, local variable values, and configuration details on any unhandled exception, leaking sensitive internal information to unauthenticated users.]

DEBUG Mode Enabled by Default with Media File Exposure — Detailed error pages leak source code, environment variables, and database credentials. Uploaded documents (medical records) served without authentication when DEBUG=True. [verified: DEBUG defaults to True with no .env override, causing verbose error pages that leak source code, env vars, and DB credentials; additionally urls.py line 14 serves media files directly without authentication when DEBUG=True.]

Hardcoded Default Database Credentials — Anyone with network access to the PostgreSQL server can authenticate with the default credentials and access all patient PII, prescriptions, and clinical records. [verified: DATABASES defaults DB_USER to 'clinic_user' and DB_PASSWORD to 'clinic_pass' (lines 65-66), the same credentials published in README.md setup instructions; no .env file exists to override them, giving anyone with network access to PostgreSQL a documented credential pair.]

Session and CSRF cookies not marked Secure when DEBUG=True — Session hijacking and CSRF token theft via network sniffing when the application is served over HTTP. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = not DEBUG and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = not DEBUG (lines 111,113) both evaluate to False because DEBUG defaults to True; session and CSRF cookies can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, enabling network sniffing.]

User Enumeration via Registration Form Error Messages — Attackers can build a list of valid usernames/emails for targeted credential-stuffing or phishing attacks against clinic patients and staff. [verified: Same PatientRegistrationForm distinct-error pattern at forms.py:27-43; the /register/ endpoint is reachable without authentication and Django renders field-level errors, enabling systematic user/email enumeration with no effective control in place.]

Account enumeration via registration reveals existing usernames and emails — An attacker can harvest valid usernames and email addresses of clinic patients and staff, enabling targeted brute-force login attacks. [verified: Same underlying code as finding 0: clean_username queries User.objects.filter(username=username).exists() and raises a distinct ValidationError at forms.py:34-37; clean_email does the same at forms.py:40-43. The /register/ endpoint is unauthenticated and no rate-limiting or generic-error control exists.]

Unrestricted file upload with no content or type validation — Upload of malicious files enabling stored XSS, malware distribution, or potential remote code execution if uploaded files are served from the web root. [verified: No file type, content, or size validation exists on the FileField (models.py:171) or DocumentForm (forms.py:186). The document_download view (views.py:676) forces Content-Disposition: attachment, which blocks stored XSS via inline rendering, but no control exists for DoS via unlimited upload size or malware distribution via forced-download of malicious executables.]

CSV formula injection in appointment export — When exported CSV is opened in a spreadsheet application, attacker-controlled formula cells execute arbitrary commands, enabling data exfiltration, command execution, or malware delivery. [verified: export_appointments writes patient names (via __str__) and reasons to CSV without sanitizing formula prefixes (=,+,-,@); both fields originate from user-supplied form input with no neutralizing control present.]

Hardcoded demo credentials in seed_data command create backdoor accounts — Known admin, clinician, front-desk, and patient credentials grant full access to the application if the seed command is executed in any non-ephemeral environment. [verified: The seed_data command hardcodes passwords (adminpass, clinicianpass, frontdeskpass, patientpass) in source code with no environment guard, confirmation prompt, or DEBUG-only gate preventing execution in non-development environments. If inadvertently run in staging or production, these known credentials become live backdoor accounts. Exploitation requires an operator with shell access to deliberate]
